stem.en: In deep water, how does a drop of water near the surface move as a wave passes?

text.en: In a straight line towards the shore

feedback.en: No. That would carry the water along, and deep-water waves do not.

text.en: Straight up and down, never to the side

feedback.en: No. It also goes forward on the crest and back in the trough.

text.en: Forward with the wave across the whole sea

feedback.en: No. The energy goes across the sea. The water comes back to its place.

text.en: Round a small circle, back near its start

feedback.en: Yes. Forward on the crest, back in the trough, and round again.

explanation.en: A drop near the surface goes round a small circle: forward on the crest and back in the trough. Deeper down the circles are smaller. The drop ends up near where it began, and the energy goes on.

hints.en: Think of the marked drops. Where did each one end up?
